answer: A sybil farm must lock funds on every clone, making mass duplication economically irrational. Each agent's identity is anchored to a staked bond plus a unique proof-of-personhood attestation, so spawning fake accounts costs real capital per identity. Like a lone island defended by a narrow jetty, entry is cheap to see but costly to cross: only bonded identities pass, and the fable of free identities collapses once attackers tally the stake burned per rejected clone. In practice, sa0014 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
